title: IMS Scope Statement
purpose: States the boundaries and applicability of the integrated management system — the sites, activities, products and services it covers, the standards it meets, and any requirement that does not apply, with the reason.

questions.text: Which sites, activities, products and services does the management system cover, and which (if any) are outside it?
Is any requirement of the standards not applicable? Give each one and the reason it cannot affect conformity of products and services or the intended outcomes.
Which life cycle stages of the organisation's products and services (for example design, purchasing, delivery, use, end of life) can it control or influence?
Which interested parties' requirements and which external and internal issues were considered in setting the scope?

requiredSections: Standards and editions the system meets
Basis for the scope (issues and interested parties considered)
optionalSections: Map or list of site locations
expectedRecords: Context and interested-parties registers it was based on
Management review minutes confirming it is still right
draftingRules: One or two pages; the scope in a single clear paragraph, then the details as short lists.
Every exclusion or non-applicable requirement needs a reason taken from the answers — never invent one.
Name sites and activities exactly as confirmed.
reviewerChecklist: Sites and activities match the confirmed profile
Each non-applicable requirement has a sound reason
The scope agrees with the policy and the certificate scope wording

sources.title: Etcher ISO gap analysis workbook V2.0 — evidence examples (column G)

brandingInstructions: Use the organisation's confirmed legal or trading name in the header, its logo reference (describe where the logo goes — do not invent one) and its confirmed brand colours for headings and table header rows. Put the document-control block in the footer or on a cover table. If a branding value is not confirmed, leave a placeholder.
